Annealing crystallises a printed bar and raises its heat deflection, never lowers it: in every same-sheet pair of an as-printed and an annealed HDT the annealed one is at least as high (the experts' 11 of 11, C24, V13). Annealing changes a printed bar's stiffness in either direction: the experts' pair sets disagree (17 of 17 rose in one; x0.79 to x1.12 in the other, C24, V13).
